text: We tested whether restricting the student's fine-tune to a low-rank adapter (LoRA rank 4) aids weak-to-strong generalization, using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 4 seeds. The weak supervisor reached 0.48 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.76. The LoRA-constrained student transferred at 0.48 accuracy (SE 0.04), yielding a performance gap recovered of -0.01 with a standard error of 0.16, against a baseline PGR of 0.11. The transfer accuracy thus matches the weak supervisor's own accuracy, indicating the student recovered essentially none of the gap between weak supervision and its own ceiling. The PGR does not exceed the baseline, and with only 4 seeds and a standard error of 0.16 the estimate is too imprecise to distinguish the low-rank condition from the baseline in either direction. These numbers do not support low-rank restriction as a beneficial intervention here; a larger seed count would be needed for any firmer reading.
